svg.title: From raw HALO exports to COMET spatial visuals
svg.desc: Eight numbered stages explain source validation, unchanged positioning, reusable counts and attributes, section measurements, animal averages, contrasts and offline visualization.

g.text: From raw HALO exports to COMET visuals
Current exploratory analysis · object rows are not independent animals
1 Original exports and explicit metadata
HALO object tables + scientist-defined animal/condition/arm mapping
Raw inputs stay local; preserve source file names and hashes.
2 Verify sources and select the cohort
Twelve completed sections; three animals per condition in each arm
Interrupted job 4978 is superseded by 5403; copies are not new animals.
3 Preserve measured object placement
Bounding-box midpoint → saved reflection/translation → aligned X/Y
No new alignment fit, physical calibration or fluorescence pixels.
4 Save reusable counts and object attributes
Four global grids + all PLA points + area/intensity/ChAT flags
Compute exact nearest neighbors across each complete section.
5 Calculate within each section and bin
Nineteen counts, fractions, sizes, intensity and spacing summaries
Empty counts/sums: assumed zero. Missing object statistics: undefined.
6 Average animals before contrasting conditions
Equal mean of defined section values → Homecage H and Running R
Three animals are available per condition; report metric-defined N.
7 Compare and retain spatial context
R − H | 100 × (R − H)/H | log₂(R/H)
Zero and missing stay distinct; retain independent observed-object context.
8 Save reports and explore in the offline app
NPZ/CSV + executed notebook + vector/600-DPI figures + bundled HTML
Fine local bins and section details; fixed 8K PNG or scalable SVG downloads.
Coverage remains uncertain. Footprint boundaries are detection context, not verified tissue masks.
